title: Why Laughter Makes Classroom Management More Effective https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2011/01/29/effective-classroom-management-and-laughter/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: In a personally-toned piece, Linsin makes the case for deliberately bringing more laughter into the classroom as a classroom management tool, not just a nice-to-have. He lists seven specific benefits: it increases teacher likeability and leverage, functions as a universal language that bridges social divides, requires little planning or effort, builds togetherness more effectively than structured community circles, motivates good behavior by making the class a place students want to belong to, eases classroom tension, and helps reach the most difficult-to-reach students. He is careful to caveat the advice, noting that humor only works as a management tool on top of already-solid classroom management fundamentals - for teachers with weak management, trying to be funny will backfire and worsen behavior.
points: Deliberate use of humor increases teacher likeability, which in turn increases behavioral leverage.
Shared laughter bridges social and emotional divides between students from different backgrounds more effectively than structured community circles.
A classroom students enjoy being part of makes exclusion (time-out) a stronger, more motivating consequence.
Humor is described as a key tool for reaching the most challenging, hardest-to-reach students.
Humor only strengthens management on top of already-solid fundamentals; for teachers with weak management it can backfire.
quotes: Laughter has the rare ability to soften hardened hearts, open shuttered minds, and endear students to one another.

When you make an effort to add humor to your lessons, routines, and activities, you instantly become more likeable to your students-which causes them to want to be around you, to please you, and to get to know you better.
Laughter is the one thing guaranteed to build camaraderie and knock down social and emotional walls, binding students from different backgrounds together into one happy classroom.
Sharing a laugh and having a good time together, however, soothes old wounds and alleviates hurt feelings better than anything else.
No student wants to wallow in time-out while their classmates are sharing a laugh with the teacher.
If you already have poor classroom management, then yes, it’s true. Trying to be funny will backfire on you. Behavior will likely get worse.
But if you have solid classroom management skills, then bringing more laughter into your classroom will make you even more effective.
